newsitem.title: USA: American Air to install new crash warning system.
newsitem.headline: American Air to install new crash warning system.

text.p: American Airlines said on Wednesday it plans to install a new crash warning system on its planes to avoid disasters like the one that killed 159 people on a flight to Colombia last December.
The new "ground-proximity warning system" sends radar signals out in front of the airplane and directly below it to prevent the aircraft from crashing into unseen land mass.

While current systems only give pilots 10-15 seconds warning of an imminent crash, American Airlines officials said the new system warns at least 60 seconds ahead. American Airlines is a unit of AMR Corp.
"This is just much better than the old system. This gives the pilot one more tool, an added safety measure," company spokesman John Hotard said.
Last December, American's Flight 965 crashed into a mountainside as it approached Cali airport in Colombia.

The crew punched in an incorrect computer code which sent the plane into a treacherous mountain range and by the time they realized the mistake, it was too late. They tried to get the plane to climb at full power but it crashed less than 300 feet (100 meters) from the mountain peak.
Hotard said the new warning system was already being looked at by American before the Cali crash, and he added that the technology could have prevented the disaster.
"Had they had a warning 60 seconds early, they would have cleared the mountain," he said. "Did Cali reaffirm or reinforce our decision? Yes it did."
Hotard said the system, designed by Allied Signal, has been certified and its use on American jets will be checked by federal regulators early next month.
The carrier plans to install the system into all of its 635 aircraft by mid-1999 at a cost of $25 million.
